statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays in the low band because Thursday's full intraday round trip and a contained futures reopen are the opposite of the mean-reversion failure the score measures, while Stress remains elevated on a multi-decade-high long-end yield rout and a 3% crude rally.
recommendation: Thursday's Nasdaq-100 cash session based at 30,204.16, roughly 0.87% below the prior close, recovered the entire decline to 30,529.35 and settled at 30,478.86, up 0.03% on the day. December NQ futures now print 30,718.00-30,721.25, about 0.15% below the 30,766.75 settle, inside a narrow 30,704.25-30,765.25 evening band on light volume of roughly 5,900 contracts. Retracements completed in both directions across a 325-point cash range and the evening book is contained, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score measures, so Tail is held at 18 in the low band. Stress stays at 56 because the macro backdrop is genuinely difficult: the 10-year Treasury yield reached about 5.22%, its highest since June 2007, the 30-year traded just shy of 5.5% and its highest since 2004, WTI settled near $94.14 after a 2.7% advance and Brent near $106.23, and roughly two-thirds odds of an October rate increase are discounted. Index internals were dispersed rather than aligned, with Meta up 4.5% and Alphabet up 1.34% against Broadcom down 1.3% and Arm down 7.88%, which undercuts the single coordinated impulse that a genuine Tail path usually requires. Confidence is 86 on fresh verified futures, index, volatility, yield, crude and calendar evidence; the shared Finviz context was about 158 minutes old and missing its futures and calendar sections, so cross-asset confirmation came from independent primary sources instead.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes flat at 30,478.86 after fully retracing a 0.87% decline; Tail holds at 18 as December NQ futures drift in a 61-point evening band
body: The Nasdaq-100 spent Thursday recovering rather than extending. Cash traded down to 30,204.16 early, about 0.87% below the 30,470.29 previous close, then worked back through the entire range to a 30,529.35 high and finished at 30,478.86, up 8.56 points. The Dow fell for a third session, down 0.31% to 51,349.98, while the S&P 500 was effectively unchanged at 7,704.13. A report that US and Iranian negotiators were working toward a phased agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for sanctions relief stalled the earlier selloff and carried the Nasdaq back into positive territory in the final hour. The dominant background remains the global long-end bond rout: the 10-year Treasury yield reached roughly 5.22%, a level last seen in June 2007, and the 30-year pushed toward 5.5%, its highest since 2004, with stronger data, higher oil and renewed inflation concern pulling additional Federal Reserve tightening into the curve. Crude added to that pressure, with WTI near $94.14 and Brent near $106.23 after gains of 2.7% and 3.4%. Volatility stayed contained: the VIX closed at 15.67 after fading from a 16.57 session high. Since the daily CME maintenance break, December NQ futures have traded a 30,704.25-30,765.25 band and print near 30,720 on light volume. That combination of completed two-way retracement, contained evening range and dispersed index internals is why the Tail estimate remains in the low band even though the Stress estimate stays elevated. The named conditions that would change the Tail reading are a renewed crude leg above Thursday's highs, a disorderly extension of the long-end move during European hours, or observed shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after Friday's 13:30Z cash open.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the Claude Tail estimate ranged from 17 to 25 and spent most of the period in the watch band. The single orange print came at 09:00Z during the European morning, when a trend-down read pushed Tail to 25. From the US cash open onward the estimate drifted back down as the index recovered its intraday decline, closing the window with four consecutive low-band readings of 19, 19, 19 and 18. Stress stayed elevated throughout, between 49 and 58, reflecting the continuing long-end yield rout rather than any observed breakdown in mean reversion.
outlookSummary: The overnight path runs through Asian and European hours with no scheduled US release until Friday's 12:30Z data block, so the conditional estimate stays in the low-to-watch band and rises mainly on liquidity transitions at the Tokyo close and European open. The concentrated window is 12:25Z to 14:15Z, covering August Durable Goods Orders at 12:30Z, the Fed Schmid speech at 13:20Z, the 13:30Z cash open and final Michigan sentiment with its five-year inflation expectation at 14:00Z. Fed Hammack speaks at 18:00Z into thinning Friday liquidity, and quarter-end rebalancing can distort the final cash hour. CME equity index futures close for the weekend at 21:00Z, after which path-dependent risk falls and Confidence steps down because no live price evidence is produced.
